introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, Advanced Level, 0710 Biology 1, June 2026. Multiple choice question paper. Duration: one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers A, B, C and D. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Use a soft HB pencil. Do all rough work in the booklet. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**Multiple choice questions** - choose the best answer, A, B, C or D.

**Directions for questions 21 to 28:** one or more of the responses (i) to (iv) is/are correct. Choose: **A** if (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct; **B** if (i) and (iii) are correct; **C** if (ii) and (iv) are correct; **D** if only (iv) is correct.

**Directions for questions 42 to 50:** there are two statements. Read through the statements and then choose: **A** if both statements are true and the second explains the first; **B** if both statements are true but the second does not explain the first; **C** if the first statement is true and the second is false; **D** if the first statement is false and the second is true.

questions.enonce_markdown: The principal form in which plant food is translocated from the leaves to storage organs or sites in plants for utilization is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Photosynthates leave the mesophyll as **sucrose**, which is loaded into the sieve tubes of the phloem. Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar, so it is chemically stable and not easily metabolised on the way; it is also very soluble and carries a lot of energy per molecule. Glucose and fructose are reducing sugars that would be used up en route, and starch is insoluble and is only a storage form. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The first acceptor of CO$_2$ fixation in C$_4$ plants is:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the mesophyll cells of C$_4$ plants, CO$_2$ (as bicarbonate) is first combined with phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP, a 3-carbon compound) in a reaction catalysed by **PEP carboxylase**, giving oxaloacetate (4 carbons). RuBP and RuBisCO belong to the Calvin cycle in the bundle sheath cells, and catalase breaks down hydrogen peroxide. Of the options, PEP carboxylase is the enzyme of the first fixation step (the acceptor molecule itself is PEP). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: This biologist coined the term CELL:
questions.corrige_markdown: In 1665 **Robert Hooke** examined thin slices of cork under a simple microscope and called the small box-like compartments "cells" (Micrographia). Virchow stated that cells arise from pre-existing cells, and Schleiden and Schwann formulated the cell theory in 1838-1839. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Retinol is an alcoholic derivative from carrots necessary in the formation of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Retinol is vitamin A. It is oxidised to retinal, which combines with the protein opsin to form **rhodopsin**, the light-sensitive pigment of the rod cells of the retina. Lack of vitamin A therefore causes night blindness. Retinol is not part of the endoplasmic reticulum, of the enzyme rennin or of the retinal membrane. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: rhodopsin in the rods of the eye.
rennin in the stomach of children.
the retinal membrane of the eye.

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of eutrophication is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Eutrophication is the enrichment of water bodies with nutrients (nitrates and phosphates from fertilisers, sewage and detergents), which makes algae and plants grow excessively, then die and be decomposed by bacteria that use up the dissolved oxygen. The example that fits is the **increase in nutrient supply in water bodies by human activities**. A decrease in nutrients, an addition of predators or a change of trophic levels is not eutrophication. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: decrease of nutrients in an ecosystem by human activities.
increase nutrient supply in water bodies by human activities.
addition of more predators in an ecosystem.
changing the trophic levels in an ecosystem by human activities.

questions.enonce_markdown: Cornified stratified squamous epithelium is found in:
questions.corrige_markdown: Stratified squamous epithelium has many layers of flat cells; in the epidermis the surface cells are filled with keratin and are dead (cornified), which makes **the skin** waterproof and resistant to abrasion. The pancreatic duct has cuboidal or columnar epithelium, the uterus has columnar epithelium, and the cheek lining is non-keratinised (moist) stratified squamous epithelium. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the cheek of the buccal cavity.

questions.enonce_markdown: The mammalian heart is said to be myogenic in action. This is brought about by the:
questions.corrige_markdown: A myogenic heart generates its own beat in the cardiac muscle, without nerve impulses starting it. The beat originates in the **sino-atrial node (SAN)**, the pacemaker in the wall of the right atrium. The vagus and sympathetic nerves only slow down or speed up the rate (they modify, not initiate); the atrioventricular node passes the excitation to the ventricles and the valves only direct the flow of blood. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Nitrogen fixing bacteria in root nodules of legume plants include:
questions.corrige_markdown: Legumes (beans, groundnuts, peas) form root nodules that contain the symbiotic bacterium ***Rhizobium***, which fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia with the enzyme nitrogenase. *Azotobacter* is a free-living nitrogen fixer, and *Nitrobacter* and *Nitrosomonas* are nitrifying bacteria, not nitrogen fixers. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The type of classification system that can be used by a forest exploiter is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A forest exploiter groups trees by their use (timber, hardwood or softwood, firewood, medicine), not by evolutionary relationship. A scheme based on one or a few convenient or useful characters is an **artificial classification**. Natural classification uses many shared features, phylogenetic classification follows evolutionary descent and phenetic classification uses overall numerical similarity. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: This tissue forms hard resilient layers in some plant parts like nuts and shells.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Sclereids** (stone cells) are short sclerenchyma cells with very thick lignified walls; they form the hard shell of nuts and the stony gritty parts of fruits such as pears. Fibres are long sclerenchyma cells that give tensile strength to stems, and tracheids and vessels are xylem elements that conduct water. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is normally used in an experiment to analyze the content and estimate the rate of flow of metabolites in phloem?
questions.corrige_markdown: A feeding aphid inserts its stylet into a single sieve tube. When the aphid is anaesthetised and cut off, the stylet stays in place and sap exudes from its cut end, so the sap can be collected and analysed and the rate of flow can be measured. This is the classical method, whereas ringing woody stems only shows that sugars move downwards in the phloem, and labelled CO$_2$ gives the pattern of movement of assimilates, not a direct sample of the sap. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If a cell has 46 chromosomes at the beginning of mitosis then at anaphase there will be a total of:
questions.corrige_markdown: At the start of mitosis the cell has 46 chromosomes, each made of two sister chromatids after replication. At anaphase the centromeres divide and the sister chromatids separate; each chromatid is now counted as a chromosome. The cell therefore has $2 \times 46 = 92$ chromosomes (46 moving to each pole). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: For a substance to qualify as an organic compound, it must have the following element.
questions.corrige_markdown: By definition an organic compound is a compound containing **carbon** (usually bonded to hydrogen), the backbone of all biological molecules. Oxygen, hydrogen and phosphorus are found in many organic compounds but are not required by the definition (for example hydrocarbons contain no oxygen or phosphorus). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which disease is a child seen to suffer from mental and physical retardation due to lack of thyroxine?
questions.corrige_markdown: Lack of thyroxine in infancy (from iodine deficiency or an under-active thyroid) causes **cretinism**: stunted growth, a low metabolic rate and poor mental development. Dwarfism comes from a lack of growth hormone, sickle cell disease is a genetic blood disorder and kwashiorkor is protein deficiency. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the reasons why "hops" is added in the process of beer making is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: In brewing, hops (the dried flowers of *Humulus lupulus*) are boiled with the wort to **impart the characteristic bitter taste** and aroma; they also act as a preservative and help clarify the wort. They do not produce gas (yeast does, during fermentation), they do not make lager and they do not increase the malt content. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The 9:3:3:1 is a ratio of:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a dihybrid cross between two double heterozygotes (for example $AaBb \times AaBb$) the offspring show four phenotypes in the ratio 9:3:3:1. It is therefore a **phenotypic ratio from a cross of individuals that differ in two traits**. The test cross gives 1:1:1:1, a monohybrid cross gives 3:1, and the genotypic ratio of a dihybrid cross is 1:2:1:2:4:2:1:2:1. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Phenotypes in a cross of individuals that differ in one trait.
Phenotypes in a cross of individuals that differ in two traits.
Genotypes in a cross of individuals that differ in two traits.

questions.enonce_markdown: Bacteria thriving in the gastrointestinal tract is an example of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Bacteria such as *Escherichia coli* in the gut feed on undigested food and in return synthesise vitamin K and some B vitamins and compete with harmful microbes: both partners benefit, which is **symbiosis** (mutualism). Inclusive fitness and balanced polymorphism are evolutionary concepts, and kin selection concerns altruism between relatives. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: This organism has a pseudocoelom.
questions.corrige_markdown: A pseudocoelom is a body cavity only partly lined by mesoderm. It is characteristic of the roundworms (phylum Nematoda), and ***Ascaris*** is a nematode. The earthworm (annelid) has a true coelom, while *Planaria* (flatworm) and the tapeworm are acoelomate flatworms. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the mammalian ear, sound is perceived in the:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sound vibrations pass through the ossicles to the oval window and set the fluid of the **cochlea** moving; the sensory hair cells of the organ of Corti convert this into nerve impulses. The semicircular canals detect rotation of the head, and the sacculus and utriculus detect position and linear movement (balance). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The position a gene occupies on a chromosome is called the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The fixed position of a gene on a chromosome is its **locus** (plural loci); alleles of the same gene occupy the same locus on homologous chromosomes. "Site", "point" and "location" are not the technical term. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Regarding the "all-or-nothing law" in nervous coordination:

- (i) the stimulus must be very high.
- (ii) occurs in neurons with myelin sheath.
- (iii) speed of transmission of impulse is low.
- (iv) the stimulus must meet up to a certain threshold value no more no less.

*Options as printed:* A) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct   B) (i) and (iii) are correct   C) (ii) and (iv) are correct   D) only (iv) is correct
questions.corrige_markdown:
The all-or-nothing law says that a neurone either fires a full action potential or does not fire at all: a stimulus below the threshold produces no impulse, and a stimulus at or above the threshold produces an impulse of the same size whatever the strength of the stimulus. (i) is false: the stimulus does not have to be very high, only to reach the threshold. (iii) is false: the law says nothing about a low speed. (iv) is true. (ii) is the doubtful one: the law applies to every axon, myelinated or not, so "occurs in neurons with myelin sheath" is true only in the sense that it also occurs there, and it is not a feature that defines the law. On the usual textbook reading only (iv) is retained; a strictly literal reading of (ii) would give C.

**Intended answer: D (only (iv) is correct).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Rodents:

- (i) have a caecum.
- (ii) have 4 stomachs.
- (iii) are herbivores.
- (iv) chew the cod.
questions.corrige_markdown: Rodents (rats, squirrels, cane rats) are mainly herbivorous gnawers with a large caecum in which symbiotic bacteria digest cellulose, so (i) and (iii) are correct. They have a simple one-chambered stomach; four stomach chambers and chewing the cud ("cud" is misprinted "cod") are features of ruminants such as cattle, so (ii) and (iv) are false. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The blood cell(s) commonly found within tissue fluid and which engulf bacteria include:

- (i) Neutrophils.
- (ii) Basophils.
- (iii) Monocytes.
- (iv) Lymphocytes.
questions.corrige_markdown: Neutrophils leave the capillaries by diapedesis and phagocytose bacteria in the tissue fluid, and monocytes become macrophages in the tissues, which also engulf bacteria. Basophils release histamine and heparin and are not phagocytic; lymphocytes produce antibodies (B cells) or kill infected cells (T cells) but do not engulf bacteria. So (i) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following about Photorespiration is correct?

- (i) It makes use of oxygen.
- (ii) It is a wasteful process.
- (iii) It is common in C$_3$ plants.
- (iv) It is carried out in bundle sheath cells.
questions.corrige_markdown: Photorespiration happens when RuBisCO fixes oxygen instead of carbon dioxide: it consumes O$_2$ (i), releases CO$_2$ and uses ATP without making sugar, so it is wasteful (ii), and it is most important in C$_3$ plants in hot, bright, dry conditions with stomata closed (iii). In C$_4$ plants the bundle sheath cells have a high CO$_2$ concentration, which suppresses photorespiration, so (iv) is false. So (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Increase in the levels of which of the following hormone(s) in the uterus will ensure that the foetus is safeguarded until birth in a mammal?

- (i) Oestrogen.
- (ii) Luteinizing hormone.
- (iii) Oxytocin.
- (iv) Progesterone.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Progesterone** maintains the thick vascular endometrium, inhibits uterine contractions and prevents ovulation and menstruation, so it keeps the foetus safe until birth (iv). Oxytocin stimulates the strong uterine contractions of labour, so a rise in oxytocin starts birth rather than preventing it (iii is false). Luteinizing hormone triggers ovulation and the formation of the corpus luteum and does not act in the uterus (ii is false). Oestrogen is also present in pregnancy, but it works with progesterone, and every option that keeps (i) also keeps (iii), which is false. The only acceptable option is therefore (iv) alone. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following characterises anaerobic reaction?

- (i) It occurs in the cytoplasm.
- (ii) The net ATP produced is 2.
- (iii) It involves mainly glycolysis.
- (iv) It uses mainly glycogen.
questions.corrige_markdown: Anaerobic respiration takes place in the cytoplasm (i), the substrate is mainly glucose, which is oxidised only by glycolysis (iii), and the net yield is 2 ATP per glucose molecule (ii). Glycogen is a storage polysaccharide that must first be hydrolysed to glucose, and it is not the main substrate, so (iv) is false. So (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Restriction endonucleases is used to:

- (i) splice DNA at specific sites.
- (ii) join okasaki DNA pieces.
- (iii) form sticky ends of DNA.
- (iv) clone bacterial cells.
questions.corrige_markdown: Restriction endonucleases recognise short palindromic base sequences and cut (splice) the DNA at those specific sites (i); many of them make staggered cuts that leave single-stranded "sticky ends" (iii). Joining Okazaki fragments is the work of DNA ligase (ii), and cloning bacterial cells is done by culture, not by restriction enzymes (iv). So (i) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is involved in dark reaction mechanism in the mammalian eye?

- (i) Rods.
- (ii) Cones.
- (iii) Rhodopsin.
- (iv) Iodopsin.
questions.corrige_markdown: In dim light (dark adaptation) vision depends on the **rods**, which contain the very sensitive pigment **rhodopsin** (visual purple), regenerated in the dark from retinal and opsin. Cones and their pigment iodopsin work in bright light and give colour vision. So (i) and (iii) are correct. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the most important causes of desertification in the Far North Region of Cameroon is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Desertification in the Sahel zone of the Far North is driven mainly by human activity: **cutting down trees and shrubs** for firewood, charcoal and farmland removes the plant cover, so the soil is exposed to wind and water erosion and loses its fertility. The Harmattan wind and overgrazing contribute, but the item points to deforestation as the main cause, and "too much wild life" is not a cause. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: cutting down of trees and shrubs.

questions.enonce_markdown: The pulse is a vital sign that measures the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The pulse is the rhythmic expansion and recoil of an artery wall each time the left ventricle ejects blood, so counting it gives the **heart rate** (beats per minute). It does not measure cardiac output (heart rate $\times$ stroke volume), blood pressure (measured with a sphygmomanometer) or the cardiac cycle itself. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these animals is classified as a filter feeder?
questions.corrige_markdown: A filter feeder strains small food particles from the water. The **mussel** (a bivalve mollusc) draws water through its gills and traps plankton in mucus on them. The earthworm is a deposit feeder, the sheep is a herbivore and the starfish is a predator that feeds on molluscs. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The presence of the waxy casparian strip within the root endodermal cells restricts the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The Casparian strip is a band of suberin (waxy) in the radial and transverse walls of the endodermal cells. It is impermeable to water, so water moving through the cell walls (the **apoplast pathway**) is blocked at the endodermis and forced into the cytoplasm (symplast), where the cell membrane can control which solutes enter the xylem. The symplast route is not restricted. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A virus that attacks bacteria is called a:
questions.corrige_markdown: A virus that infects and multiplies inside bacterial cells is a **bacteriophage**, or phage virus (for example the T4 phage). A retrovirus has an RNA genome that is copied into DNA (as HIV does), "DNA virus" is only a type by genetic material and "virulent virus" describes a pathogenic virus. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mechanical breakdown of food is one function of the:
questions.corrige_markdown: In birds the **gizzard** has thick muscular walls and contains grit that grinds the food. The crop only stores food, the liver makes bile (which emulsifies fats but does not grind food) and the rumen is the fermentation chamber where microbes digest cellulose. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A lichen is a symbiotic association between a:
questions.corrige_markdown: A lichen is a mutualistic association of a **fungus and an alga** (or a cyanobacterium): the alga makes food by photosynthesis, and the fungus gives protection, water and mineral salts. The other pairs are a cow and egret (commensalism), man and *E. coli* (mutualism in the gut) and crab and sea anemone (a different association). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Rounded bacteria that form chains of colonies is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Rounded (spherical) bacteria are cocci; when the cells stay attached in a **chain** after division they are **streptococci**. Staphylococci form grape-like clusters, diplococci occur in pairs and *Sarcina* forms packets of four or eight cells. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which molecule is involved in the process of transcription?
questions.corrige_markdown: Transcription is the synthesis of **mRNA** from the template strand of DNA by RNA polymerase, so mRNA is the molecule made in the process. DNA polymerase and DNA ligase are enzymes of DNA replication, and helicase unwinds DNA in replication. RNA polymerase itself is not among the options. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which part of the kidney nephron does absorption of glucose from the glomerular filtrate occur?
questions.corrige_markdown: All the glucose in the glomerular filtrate is reabsorbed by active transport in the cells of the **proximal convoluted tubule**, which have microvilli and many mitochondria, so normally no glucose appears in the urine. The collecting duct and the distal tubule regulate water and ions, and Bowman's capsule only collects the filtrate. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A coenzyme has which of the following two properties?

| Option | Nature | Binding to the enzyme |
|---|---|---|
| A | Protein in nature | Tightly bound to the enzyme |
| B | Organic in nature | Loosely bound to the enzyme |
| C | Metal ion in nature | Tightly bound to the enzyme |
| D | Protein in nature | Loosely bound to the enzyme |
questions.corrige_markdown: A coenzyme is a small **non-protein organic** molecule (often derived from a vitamin, for example NAD from nicotinamide) that is only **loosely bound** to the enzyme and can be released and reused. A tightly bound organic cofactor is a prosthetic group, and a metal ion is an inorganic cofactor or activator. No coenzyme is a protein. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Protein in nature, tightly bound to the enzyme.
Organic in nature, loosely bound to the enzyme.
Metal ion in nature, tightly bound to the enzyme.
Protein in nature, loosely bound to the enzyme.

questions.enonce_markdown: By definition the arteries carry:
questions.corrige_markdown: Arteries are defined by the direction of flow: they carry blood **away from the heart**. This blood is usually oxygenated (the pulmonary artery is the exception and carries deoxygenated blood), and blood towards the heart travels in veins. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following phyla is saprophytic?
questions.corrige_markdown: Saprophytes feed on dead organic matter by secreting enzymes and absorbing the products. **Basidiomycota** (mushrooms, toadstools, bracket fungi) are fungi that live as saprophytes. Bryophytes are autotrophic, Ciliata are protozoa that ingest food and Rhizopoda (amoeba) are holozoic. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Fossil evidences are not taken seriously because of missing links.

**Second statement:** Fossils are rare occurrences in nature.
questions.corrige_markdown: Fossils are rare because dead organisms are usually eaten or decomposed, and only a few are buried quickly in sediments and fossilised; the fossil record is therefore incomplete, which produces the gaps ("missing links") between groups. The second statement is true, and it explains why there are missing links, the reason given in the first statement for doubting the fossil evidence. On that reading both statements are true and the second explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
The first statement is true and the second is false
The first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** A small interbreeding population within a species constitutes a deme.

**Second statement:** Each deme has its own gene pool.
questions.corrige_markdown: A deme is a small local interbreeding population of a species, and all the alleles of its members form the deme's gene pool, so both statements are true. The deme is defined by its members interbreeding with each other, not by having a separate gene pool: the gene pool is a property that follows from it, so the second statement does not explain the first. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
The first statement is true and the second is false
The first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** In the equatorial forest, heat stroke is rare because of much rainfall.

**Second statement:** The weather in the equatorial forest makes it hard for evaporation of water resulting in cooling.
questions.corrige_markdown: The air of the equatorial forest is very humid, so sweat evaporates slowly and the cooling it gives is poor: the body loses heat badly and heat stroke is common there, not rare. The first statement is therefore false (and rainfall is not what prevents it). The second statement is true: high humidity reduces evaporation of sweat, and so the cooling. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
The first statement is true and the second is false
The first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** The greenhouse effect causes global warming.

**Second statement:** Global warming melts polar ice into the oceans.
questions.corrige_markdown: Gases such as CO$_2$ and methane trap heat in the atmosphere (the greenhouse effect) and raise the mean temperature of the Earth (global warming), so the first statement is true. Global warming melts polar ice and raises sea level, so the second is true too, but it is a consequence of global warming and not an explanation of why the greenhouse effect causes it. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
The first statement is true and the second is false
The first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** The lady bird beetle is used in biological control in a garden.

**Second statement:** Lady bird beetle preys on aphids in a garden.
questions.corrige_markdown: Biological control uses a natural enemy to keep a pest down. The ladybird (ladybug) beetle and its larvae eat aphids, which damage garden plants, and this predation is the reason why the beetle is used. Both statements are true and the second explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
The first statement is true and the second is false
The first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Potassium cyanide is a very potent respiratory poison.

**Second statement:** Potassium cyanide reacts irreversibly with the active site of cytochrome oxidase.
questions.corrige_markdown: Cyanide binds to the iron of cytochrome oxidase, the last carrier of the electron transport chain, and blocks the transfer of electrons to oxygen, so oxidative phosphorylation and ATP synthesis stop and cells die. It is for that reason a very potent respiratory poison. Both statements are true and the second explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
The first statement is true and the second is false
The first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** The nitrogenous waste of a marine teleost is trimethyl amine oxide.

**Second statement:** Trimethyl amine oxide requires little amounts of water for its elimination.
questions.corrige_markdown: Marine bony fish (teleosts) live in water that is more concentrated than their blood, so they lose water by osmosis and must save it. In textbooks they excrete part of their nitrogenous waste as trimethylamine oxide (TMAO), a compound of low toxicity that needs little water to be removed, together with some ammonia. Both statements are true and the second explains why TMAO suits a marine teleost. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
The first statement is true and the second is false

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Alcohol in the blood increase diuresis in Mammals.

**Second statement:** Alcohol in the blood stimulates increase production of ADH into the blood.
questions.corrige_markdown: Alcohol inhibits the release of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) by the posterior pituitary, so the collecting ducts stay impermeable to water, much water is lost and a large volume of dilute urine is produced (diuresis). The first statement is true, but the second statement is false: alcohol decreases ADH production, and does not stimulate it. **Answer: C.**

**First statement:** During muscle contraction the sarcomere length increases.

**Second statement:** During muscle contraction the globular head of the thick myosin myofilaments enables cross bridge formation.
questions.corrige_markdown: In the sliding filament mechanism the myosin heads bind to actin and form cross bridges, then pivot and pull the thin filaments towards the centre of the sarcomere (second statement true). As a result the sarcomere becomes **shorter** (the I band and H zone narrow, the A band stays the same), so the first statement is false. **Answer: D.**
